messages:
Maria: Hey team — noticing the Android sample app sometimes re-uploads files twice when network blips happen during onboarding. Seen this in Crashlytics and a few customer reports.
Kevin: Ugh. Is this the streaming upload flow we added for the sample?
Maria: Yeah, using Retrofit + OkHttp with a custom RequestBody that streams from a FileDescriptor. If a call times out and OkHttp retries, the body can't be replayed so it ends up doing a second upload later.
Anya: Do we have retries enabled at the OkHttp level? I thought we set retryOnConnectionFailure = true for most clients.
Kevin: We do. For most idempotent calls that's fine. But streaming file uploads are not idempotent.
Sam: Repro steps I used: 1) Launch sample app on emulator. 2) Start a ~6MB upload. 3) Toggle airplane mode for ~2s while upload is running, then turn back on. 4) Watch logs — you see the first call fail with a timeout, then shortly after a second POST with same body starts.
Maria: Logs excerpt: ```
I/okhttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.local/v1/upload
I/okhttp: --> END POST (streamed)
I/okhttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: timeout
I/okhttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.local/v1/upload
I/okhttp: --> END POST (streamed)
```
Anya: Looks like OkHttp is transparently retrying the call. For streamed bodies it prints "(streamed)" which means it can't be buffered and retried safely.
Kevin: There's an OkHttp behavior where it will retry certain connection failures even if the body is one-shot. But if the call fails before the body is fully transmitted, the retry might still attempt to re-send — leading to duplicate uploads.
Sam: Quick patch idea: make our Retrofit client set retryOnConnectionFailure = false for the sample app's upload client. That should stop automatic retries.
Maria: That would mitigate the sample app but we should also fix SDK defaults. Developers will copy our sample config.
Anya: Agreed. Proposal: SDK should detect non-repeatable request bodies and disable automatic retries for those calls by default. Also expose an opt-in flag in the client builder for "allowStreamingRetries".
Kevin: Implementation sketch: check for RequestBody that returns contentLength() == -1 or marks itself as "one-shot". If so, set call.tag(OneShotUpload::class.java) and our dispatcher should skip automatic retries for tagged calls.
Maria: Example (pseudo-Kotlin):
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true) // default
  .addInterceptor { chain ->
    val req = chain.request()
    if (isNonRepeatable(req.body)) {
      // mark so retry logic can read it
      req.newBuilder().tag(OneShot::class.java, OneShot()).build()
    }
    chain.proceed(req)
  }
  .build()

// in our retry policy: skip retries if request.tag(OneShot::class.java) != null
```
Sam: I like it. Also we should add a sample app test that uses the emulator network toggle to assert only one POST observed by the test server.
Anya: For the short term we should patch the sample app config to disable retries and call it out in README onboarding steps.
Maria: I'll open a PR to change the sample app client and add a unit/integration test.
Kevin: Could also add a warning in the SDK docs: "If your request body is streamed and cannot be replayed, ensure retries are disabled or handle de-duplication server-side."
ci-bot: CI pipeline started for branch fix/sample-upload-retries (build 4821).
Maria: Thanks — assigning to me. I'll include log snippets and the reproduction emulator script in the PR.
Anya: Nice. After Maria's PR we should schedule a quick eng-ship to update the sample app on the docs site and the quickstart repo.
Sam: One edge case — multipart with mixed parts (some repeatable, one streamed). We should treat the whole request as non-repeatable.
Kevin: Good call. Make isNonRepeatable conservative: if any part is non-repeatable, mark whole request one-shot.
Maria: Filed GH issue #8142 for SDK change + #8143 for sample update. Will link PRs here when ready.
